subject: ITF
body: What is the FIRST step in the standard troubleshooting methodology?
options: Establish a theory of probable cause
explanation: Identify the problem → theory → test → plan → implement → verify → document.

subject: ITF
body: After fixing a fault, what should a technician do before closing the ticket?
options: Verify full system functionality and document the fix
explanation: Verify the fix and implement preventive measures, then document.

subject: ITF
body: A theory of probable cause is confirmed. What comes next?
options: Establish a plan of action to resolve the problem
explanation: Then implement the plan or escalate.

subject: ITF
body: A user says 'the internet is down'. Others on the same network are fine. What is the most sensible next check?
options: Check that user's own connection, cable or Wi-Fi settings
explanation: If only one user is affected, start at their device.

subject: ITF
body: A PC shows 'No boot device found' after a new SSD was installed. What is the most likely cause?
options: The boot order or the drive connection/installation
explanation: The firmware cannot find a bootable drive.

subject: ITF
body: A laptop runs on battery but won't charge when plugged in. What should you check first?
options: The charger, cable and power outlet
explanation: Check the simplest, most likely cause first.

subject: ITF
body: Which Windows tool shows running processes and lets you end a frozen program?
explanation: Open it with Ctrl+Shift+Esc.

subject: ITF
body: Which Windows tool is used to update or roll back a device driver?
explanation: Right-click the device → Properties → Driver.

subject: ITF
body: Which Windows tool shows system and application logs for diagnosing errors?
explanation: Logs are grouped into Application, Security and System.

subject: ITF
body: Which Windows command shows the computer's IP configuration?
explanation: Use ipconfig /all for full details. Linux uses ip addr (or ifconfig).

subject: ITF
body: Which Linux command lists files in a directory?
explanation: pwd prints the current directory; cd changes it.

subject: ITF
body: Which Linux command changes file permissions?
explanation: chown changes ownership; sudo runs a command as another user (often root).

subject: ITF
body: Which file system is the default for modern Windows system drives?
explanation: ext4 is common on Linux and APFS on macOS.

subject: ITF
body: What is the main limitation of the FAT32 file system?
options: A maximum single file size of 4 GB
It can't be read by Windows
explanation: exFAT removes this limit for removable drives.

subject: ITF
body: Software you can use for free but whose source code is not shared is called
explanation: Open-source software publishes its source code.

subject: ITF
body: Which type of licence lets anyone view, modify and share the source code?
explanation: Examples include Linux and LibreOffice.

subject: ITF
body: What does MFA require?
options: Two or more different types of authentication factor
explanation: Factors: something you know, have, or are.

subject: ITF
body: An email urges you to 'verify your account' via a link to a lookalike site. This is
explanation: Report it and don't click the link.

subject: ITF
body: Which malware encrypts files and demands payment?
explanation: Good backups are the main defence.

subject: ITF
body: The principle of least privilege means
options: users get only the access they need to do their job
explanation: It limits damage from mistakes and compromised accounts.

subject: ITF
body: Which backup rule recommends 3 copies, on 2 types of media, with 1 off-site?
explanation: It protects against device failure, disasters and ransomware.

subject: ITF
body: Someone follows an employee through a secure door without badging in. This is
explanation: Shoulder surfing is watching someone type a PIN or password.

subject: ITF
body: Which service turns a website name into an IP address?
explanation: DHCP assigns addresses; DNS resolves names.

subject: ITF
body: An IP address starting 169.254 on Windows usually means
options: the DNS server is down only
the device has a static public IP
the device could not reach a DHCP server
explanation: It's an APIPA (link-local) address.

subject: ITF
body: Which Wi-Fi security standard is the newest and strongest?
explanation: WEP is broken and should never be used.

subject: ITF
body: What does a router mainly do?
explanation: A switch connects devices within the same network.

subject: ITF
body: Which cable connector is used for wired Ethernet?
explanation: RJ11 is for telephone lines.

subject: ITF
body: Which cloud model provides ready-to-use applications such as webmail?
explanation: IaaS provides virtual machines; PaaS provides a platform to build apps.

subject: ITF
body: Which cloud model provides virtual machines, storage and networks you manage yourself?
explanation: You manage the OS and apps; the provider manages hardware.

subject: ITF
body: Which RAID level mirrors data across two drives?
explanation: RAID 0 stripes with no redundancy; RAID 5 uses parity across 3+ drives.

subject: ITF
body: Which RAID level stripes data for speed but gives NO fault tolerance?
explanation: If one drive fails, all data is lost.

subject: ITF
body: Which port is most commonly used to connect a modern monitor?
explanation: VGA is legacy analogue.

subject: ITF
body: A thermal paste problem would most likely cause the computer to
options: overheat and shut down or throttle
explanation: Thermal paste transfers heat from the CPU to the cooler.

subject: ITF
body: What is an SLA in IT support?
options: An agreement setting the expected service levels, such as response times
explanation: Service Level Agreement.

subject: ITF
body: When should a technician escalate a ticket?
options: Only if the user is angry
When the issue is beyond their knowledge, access or authority
explanation: Escalate with notes of what was already tried.

subject: ITF
body: Before making a major change on a user's PC, a technician should first
options: make sure the user's data is backed up
explanation: Protect data before risky changes.

explanation: The CPU processes instructions and performs calculations.

explanation: The RAM temporarily holds data and programs currently in use and is cleared when power is lost.

subject: ITF

explanation: The SSD stores data permanently using flash memory with no moving parts.

subject: ITF

explanation: The HDD stores data permanently on spinning magnetic platters.

subject: ITF

subject: ITF

subject: ITF

subject: ITF

explanation: Memory uses binary units: 1 GB = 1,024 MB, so 16 × 1,024 = 16384 MB.
